10.6.e: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

10.6.s: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā anuruddho rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya dhammapadāni bhāsati. Atha kho piyaṅkaramātā yakkhinī puttakaṁ evaṁ tosesi:
10.6.e: Now at that time Venerable Anuruddha rose at the crack of dawn and recited passages of the teaching. Then the native spirit Piyaṅkara’s Mother soothed her little child, saying:

10.6.s:
“Mā saddaṁ kari piyaṅkara,
Bhikkhu dhammapadāni bhāsati;
Api ca dhammapadaṁ vijāniya,
Paṭipajjema hitāya no siyā.
10.6.e:
“Don’t make a sound, Piyaṅkara!
A mendicant recites passages of the teaching.
When we understand a passage,
we can practice for our welfare.

10.6.s:
Pāṇesu ca saṁyamāmase,
Sampajānamusā na bhaṇāmase;
Sikkhema susīlyamattano,
Api muccema pisācayoniyā”ti.
10.6.e:
Let us restrain ourselves from harming living creatures,
and speak no lying words.
We should train ourselves well in ethics,
and hopefully we’ll be freed from the goblin realm.”

10.7.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
10.7.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

10.7.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā bhikkhū nibbānapaṭisaṁyuttāya dhammiyā kathāya sandasseti samādapeti samuttejeti sampahaṁseti. Te ca bhikkhū aṭṭhiṁ katvā manasi katvā sabbacetasā samannāharitvā ohitasotā dhammaṁ suṇanti.
10.7.e: Now at that time the Buddha was educating, encouraging, firing up, and inspiring the mendicants with a Dhamma talk about extinguishment. And those mendicants were paying attention, applying the mind, concentrating wholeheartedly, and actively listening.

10.7.s: Atha kho punabbasumātā yakkhinī puttake evaṁ tosesi:
10.7.e: Then the native spirit Punabbasu’s Mother soothed her little children, saying:

10.7.s:
“Tuṇhī uttarike hohi,
tuṇhī hohi punabbasu;
Yāvāhaṁ buddhaseṭṭhassa,
dhammaṁ sossāmi satthuno.
10.7.e:
“Hush, little Uttarā!
Hush, Punabbasu!
For I want to listen to the teaching
of the Teacher, the supreme Buddha.

10.7.s:
Nibbānaṁ bhagavā āha,
sabbaganthappamocanaṁ;
Ativelā ca me hoti,
asmiṁ dhamme piyāyanā.
10.7.e:
Extinguishment, the Blessed One said,
is the release from all ties.
I have a lasting love
for this teaching.

10.7.s:
Piyo loke sako putto,
piyo loke sako pati;
Tato piyatarā mayhaṁ,
assa dhammassa magganā.

Na hi putto pati vāpi,
piyo dukkhā pamocaye;
Yathā saddhammassavanaṁ,
dukkhā moceti pāṇinaṁ.
10.7.e:
For neither son nor husband,
dear as they are, can free you from suffering;
as listening to the true teaching
frees living creatures from suffering.

In this world mired in suffering,
fettered by old age and death,
I want to listen to the teaching
through which the Buddha awakened,
which frees you from old age and death.
So hush, Punabbasu!”

“Mom, I’m not speaking,
and Uttarā is silent, too.
Focus just on the teaching,
for it’s nice to listen to the true teaching.
And it’s because we haven’t understood the teaching
that we live in suffering, Mom.

10.7.s:
Esa devamanussānaṁ,
sammūḷhānaṁ pabhaṅkaro;
Buddho antimasārīro,
dhammaṁ deseti cakkhumā”ti.
10.7.e:
He is a beacon for those who are lost
among gods and humans.
The Buddha, bearing his final body,
the Clear-eyed One teaches Dhamma.”

10.7.s:
“Sādhu kho paṇḍito nāma,
putto jāto uresayo;
Putto me buddhaseṭṭhassa,
dhammaṁ suddhaṁ piyāyati.
10.7.e:
“It’s good that my child’s so astute,
this child I bore and suckled!
My child loves the pure teaching
of the supreme Buddha.

10.7.s:
Punabbasu sukhī hohi,
ajjāhamhi samuggatā;
Diṭṭhāni ariyasaccāni,
uttarāpi suṇātu me”ti.
10.7.e:
Punabbasu, may you be happy!
Today, I rise.
Hear me too, Uttarā:
I have seen the noble truths!”

10.8.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati sītavane.
10.8.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Cool Grove.

10.8.s: Tena kho pana samayena anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati rājagahaṁ anuppatto hoti kenacideva karaṇīyena. Assosi kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati: “buddho kira loke uppanno”ti.
10.8.e: Now at that time the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had arrived at Rājagaha on some business. He heard a rumor that a Buddha had arisen in the world.

10.8.s: Tāvadeva ca pana bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamitukāmo hoti. Athassa anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa etadahosi: “akālo kho ajja bhagavantaṁ dassanāya upasaṅkamituṁ. Sve dānāhaṁ kālena bhagavantaṁ dassanāya gamissāmī”ti buddhagatāya satiyā nipajji.
10.8.e: Right away he wanted to go and see the Buddha, but he thought, “It’s too late to go and see the Buddha today. I’ll go and see him tomorrow.” He went to bed thinking of the Buddha.

10.8.s: Rattiyā sudaṁ tikkhattuṁ vuṭṭhāsi pabhātanti maññamāno. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena sivathikadvāraṁ tenupasaṅkami. Amanussā dvāraṁ vivariṁsu.
10.8.e: During the night he got up three times thinking it was sunup. Then he approached the Sivaka Gate, and non-human beings opened it for him.

10.8.s: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa nagaramhā nikkhamantassa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro pāturahosi, bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁso udapādi, tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi.
10.8.e: But as he was leaving the city, light vanished and darkness appeared to him. He felt fear, terror, and goosebumps, and wanted to turn back.

10.8.s: Atha kho sivako yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi:
10.8.e: Then the invisible spirit Sivaka called out:

“A hundred elephants, a hundred horses,
a hundred mule-drawn chariots,
a hundred thousand maidens
bedecked with jeweled earrings:
these are not worth a sixteenth part
of a single forward stride!

10.8.s:
Abhikkama gahapati,
abhikkama gahapati;
Abhikkamanaṁ te seyyo,
no paṭikkamanan”ti.
10.8.e:
Forward, householder!
Forward, householder!
Going forward is better for you,
not turning back!”

10.8.s: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi, āloko pāturahosi, yaṁ ahosi bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁso, so paṭippassambhi.
10.8.e: Then darkness vanished and light appeared to Anāthapiṇḍika. His fear, terror, and goosebumps settled down.

10.8.s: Dutiyampi kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro pāturahosi, bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁso udapādi, tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi.
10.8.e: But for a second time, light vanished and darkness appeared to him. …

10.8.s: Dutiyampi kho sivako yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi:
10.8.e: For a second time the invisible spirit Sivaka called out …

10.8.s:
“Sataṁ hatthī sataṁ assā,
…pe…
Kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ.

Abhikkama gahapati,
abhikkama gahapati;
Abhikkamanaṁ te seyyo,
no paṭikkamanan”ti.
10.8.e:
“… Going forward is better for you,
not turning back!”

10.8.s: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi, āloko pāturahosi, yaṁ ahosi bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁso, so paṭippassambhi.
10.8.e: Then darkness vanished and light appeared to Anāthapiṇḍika. His fear, terror, and goosebumps settled down.

10.8.s: Tatiyampi kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa āloko antaradhāyi, andhakāro pāturahosi, bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁso udapādi, tatova puna nivattitukāmo ahosi.
10.8.e: But for a third time, light vanished and darkness appeared to him. …

10.8.s: Tatiyampi kho sivako yakkho antarahito saddamanussāvesi:
10.8.e: For a third time the invisible spirit Sivaka called out …

10.8.s:
“Sataṁ hatthī sataṁ assā,
…pe…
Kalaṁ nāgghanti soḷasiṁ.

Abhikkama gahapati,
abhikkama gahapati;
Abhikkamanaṁ te seyyo,
no paṭikkamanan”ti.
10.8.e:
“… Going forward is better for you,
not turning back!”

10.8.s: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa andhakāro antaradhāyi, āloko pāturahosi, yaṁ ahosi bhayaṁ chambhitattaṁ lomahaṁso, so paṭippassambhi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena sītavanaṁ yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami.
10.8.e: Then darkness vanished and light appeared to Anāthapiṇḍika. His fear, terror, and goosebumps settled down. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went to the Cool Grove and approached the Buddha.

10.8.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā rattiyā paccūsasamayaṁ paccuṭṭhāya abbhokāse caṅkamati. Addasā kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ. Disvāna caṅkamā orohitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṁ gahapatiṁ etadavoca: “ehi, sudattā”ti.
10.8.e: Now at that time the Buddha had risen at the crack of dawn and was walking mindfully in the open. He saw Anāthapiṇḍika coming off in the distance. So he stepped down from the walking path, sat down on the seat spread out, and said to Anāthapiṇḍika, “Come, Sudatta.”

10.8.s: Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati, nāmena maṁ bhagavā ālapatīti, haṭṭho udaggo tattheva bhagavato pādesu sirasā nipatitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “kacci, bhante, bhagavā sukhamasayitthā”ti?
10.8.e: Then Anāthapiṇḍika thought, “The Buddha calls me by name!” Smiling and elated, he bowed with his head to the Buddha’s feet and said to him, “Sir, I trust the Buddha slept well?”

10.8.s:
“Sabbadā ve sukhaṁ seti,
brāhmaṇo parinibbuto;
Yo na limpati kāmesu,
sītibhūto nirūpadhi.
10.8.e:
“A brahmin who is fully quenched
always sleeps at ease.
Sensual pleasures slip off them,
they’re cooled, free of attachments.

10.8.s:
Sabbā āsattiyo chetvā,
vineyya hadaye daraṁ;
Upasanto sukhaṁ seti,
santiṁ pappuyya cetasā”ti.
10.8.e:
Since they’ve cut off all clinging,
and removed the stress from the heart,
the peaceful sleep at ease,
having found peace of mind.”

10.9.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
10.9.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

10.9.s: Tena kho pana samayena sukkā bhikkhunī mahatiyā parisāya parivutā dhammaṁ deseti. Atha kho sukkāya bhikkhuniyā abhippasanno yakkho rājagahe rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ upasaṅkamitvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
10.9.e: Now, at that time the nun Sukkā was teaching Dhamma, surrounded by a large assembly. Then a native spirit was so devoted to Sukkā that he went from street to street and from square to square, and on that occasion recited these verses:

10.9.s:
“Kiṁ me katā rājagahe manussā,
Madhupītāva seyare;
Ye sukkaṁ na payirupāsanti,
Desentiṁ amataṁ padaṁ.
10.9.e:
“What’s up with these people in Rājagaha?
They sleep like they’ve been drinking mead!
They don’t attend on Sukkā
as she’s teaching the state free of death.

10.9.s:
Tañca pana appaṭivānīyaṁ,
Asecanakamojavaṁ;
Pivanti maññe sappaññā,
Valāhakamiva panthagū”ti.
10.9.e:
But the wise—
it’s as if they drink it up,
so irresistible, delectable, and nutritious,
like travelers enjoying a cool cloud.”

10.10.s: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
10.10.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

10.10.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako sukkāya bhikkhuniyā bhojanaṁ adāsi. Atha kho sukkāya bhikkhuniyā abhippasanno yakkho rājagahe rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ upasaṅkamitvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
10.10.e: Now at that time a certain lay follower gave food to the nun Sukkā. Then a native spirit was so devoted to Sukkā that he went from street to street and from square to square, and on that occasion recited these verses:

10.10.s:
“Puññaṁ vata pasavi bahuṁ,
Sappañño vatāyaṁ upāsako;
Yo sukkāya adāsi bhojanaṁ,
Sabbaganthehi vippamuttiyā”ti.
10.10.e:
“O! He has made so much merit!
That lay follower is so very wise.
He just gave food to Sukkā,
who is released from all ties.”

10.11.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe.
10.11.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.

10.11.s: Tena kho pana samayena aññataro upāsako cīrāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaraṁ adāsi. Atha kho cīrāya bhikkhuniyā abhippasanno yakkho rājagahe rathikāya rathikaṁ siṅghāṭakena siṅghāṭakaṁ upasaṅkamitvā tāyaṁ velāyaṁ imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
10.11.e: Now at that time a certain lay follower gave a robe to the nun Cīrā. Then a native spirit was so devoted to Cīrā that he went from street to street and from square to square, and on that occasion recited these verses:

10.11.s:
“Puññaṁ vata pasavi bahuṁ,
Sappañño vatāyaṁ upāsako;
Yo cīrāya adāsi cīvaraṁ,
Sabbayogehi vippamuttiyā”ti.
10.11.e:
“O! He has made so much merit!
That lay-follower is so very wise.
He gave a robe to Cīrā,
who is released from all yokes.”

10.12.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā āḷaviyaṁ viharati āḷavakassa yakkhassa bhavane.
10.12.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Āḷavī in the haunt of the native spirit Āḷavaka.

10.12.s: Atha kho āḷavako yakkho yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti.
10.12.e: Then the native spirit Āḷavaka went up to the Buddha, and said to him: “Get out, ascetic!”

10.12.s: “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā nikkhami.
10.12.e: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went out.

10.12.s: “Pavisa, samaṇā”ti.
10.12.e: “Get in, ascetic!”

10.12.s: “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā pāvisi.
10.12.e: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went in.

10.12.s: Dutiyampi kho āḷavako yakkho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti.
10.12.e: And for a second time the native spirit Āḷavaka said to the Buddha, “Get out, ascetic!”

10.12.s: “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā nikkhami.
10.12.e: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went out.

10.12.s: “Pavisa, samaṇā”ti.
10.12.e: “Get in, ascetic!”

10.12.s: “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā pāvisi.
10.12.e: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went in.

10.12.s: Tatiyampi kho āḷavako yakkho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti.
10.12.e: And for a third time the native spirit Āḷavaka said to the Buddha, “Get out, ascetic!”

10.12.s: “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā nikkhami.
10.12.e: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went out.

10.12.s: “Pavisa, samaṇā”ti.
10.12.e: “Get in, ascetic!”

10.12.s: “Sādhāvuso”ti bhagavā pāvisi.
10.12.e: Saying, “All right, respectable sir,” the Buddha went in.

10.12.s: Catutthampi kho āḷavako yakkho bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
10.12.e: And for a fourth time the native spirit Āḷavaka said to the Buddha,

10.12.s: “nikkhama, samaṇā”ti.
10.12.e: “Get out, ascetic!”

10.12.s: “Na khvāhaṁ taṁ, āvuso, nikkhamissāmi. Yaṁ te karaṇīyaṁ taṁ karohī”ti.
10.12.e: “No, respectable sir, I won’t get out. Do what you must.”

10.12.s: “Pañhaṁ taṁ, samaṇa, pucchissāmi. Sace me na byākarissasi, cittaṁ vā te khipissāmi, hadayaṁ vā te phālessāmi, pādesu vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya khipissāmī”ti.
10.12.e: “I will ask you a question, ascetic. If you don’t answer me, I’ll drive you insane, or explode your heart, or grab you by the feet and throw you to the far shore of the Ganges!”

10.12.s: “Na khvāhaṁ taṁ, āvuso, passāmi sadevake loke samārake sabrahmake sassamaṇabrāhmaṇiyā pajāya sadevamanussāya, yo me cittaṁ vā khipeyya hadayaṁ vā phāleyya, pādesu vā gahetvā pāragaṅgāya khipeyya. Api ca tvaṁ, āvuso, puccha yadā kaṅkhasī”ti (…).
10.12.e: “I don’t see anyone in this world with its gods, Māras, and divinities, this population with its ascetics and brahmins, its gods and humans who could do that to me. But anyway, ask what you wish.”

10.12.s:
“Kiṁsūdha vittaṁ purisassa seṭṭhaṁ,
Kiṁsu suciṇṇaṁ sukhamāvahāti;
Kiṁsu have sādutaraṁ rasānaṁ,
Kathaṁjīviṁ jīvitamāhu seṭṭhan”ti.
10.12.e:
“What’s a person’s best wealth?
What brings happiness when practiced well?
What’s the sweetest taste of all?
The one they say has the best life: how do they live?”

10.12.s:
“Saddhīdha vittaṁ purisassa seṭṭhaṁ,
Dhammo suciṇṇo sukhamāvahāti;
Saccaṁ have sādutaraṁ rasānaṁ,
Paññājīviṁ jīvitamāhu seṭṭhan”ti.
10.12.e:
“Faith here is a person’s best wealth.
The teaching brings happiness when practiced well.
Truth is the sweetest taste of all.
The one they say has the best life lives by wisdom.”

10.12.s:
“Kathaṁsu tarati oghaṁ,
kathaṁsu tarati aṇṇavaṁ;
Kathaṁsu dukkhamacceti,
kathaṁsu parisujjhatī”ti.
10.12.e:
“How do you cross the flood?
How do you cross the deluge?
How do you get over suffering?
How do you get purified?”

10.12.s:
“Saddhāya tarati oghaṁ,
appamādena aṇṇavaṁ;
Vīriyena dukkhamacceti,
paññāya parisujjhatī”ti.
10.12.e:
“By faith you cross the flood,
and by diligence the deluge.
By energy you get past suffering,
and you’re purified by wisdom.”

“How do you get wisdom?
How do you earn wealth?
How do you get a good reputation?
How do you hold on to friends?
How do the departed not grieve
when passing from this world to the next?”

10.12.s:
“Saddahāno arahataṁ,
dhammaṁ nibbānapattiyā;
Sussūsaṁ labhate paññaṁ,
appamatto vicakkhaṇo.
10.12.e:
“One who is diligent and discerning
gains wisdom by wanting to learn,
having faith in the perfected ones,
and the teaching for becoming extinguished.

Being responsible, acting appropriately,
and working hard you earn wealth.
Truthfulness wins you a good reputation.
You hold on to friends by giving.
That’s how the departed do not grieve
when passing from this world to the next.

10.12.s:
Yassete caturo dhammā,
saddhassa gharamesino;
Saccaṁ dhammo dhiti cāgo,
sa ve pecca na socati.
10.12.e:
A faithful householder of discernment
who possesses these four qualities
does not grieve after passing away:
truth, principle, steadfastness, and generosity.

10.12.s:
Iṅgha aññepi pucchassu,
puthū samaṇabrāhmaṇe;
Yadi saccā dhammā cāgā,
khantyā bhiyyodha vijjatī”ti.
10.12.e:
Go ahead, ask others as well,
there are many ascetics and brahmins.
See whether anything better is found
than truth, principle, generosity, and patience.”

10.12.s:
“Kathaṁ nu dāni puccheyyaṁ,
puthū samaṇabrāhmaṇe;
Yohaṁ ajja pajānāmi,
yo attho samparāyiko.
10.12.e:
“Why now would I question
the many ascetics and brahmins?
Today I understand
what’s good for lives to come.

10.12.s:
Atthāya vata me buddho,
vāsāyāḷavimāgamā;
Yohaṁ ajja pajānāmi,
yattha dinnaṁ mahapphalaṁ.
10.12.e:
It was truly for my benefit
that the Buddha came to stay at Āḷavī.
Today I understand
where a gift is very fruitful.

10.12.s:
So ahaṁ vicarissāmi,
Gāmā gāmaṁ purā puraṁ;
Namassamāno sambuddhaṁ,
Dhammassa ca sudhammatan”ti.
10.12.e:
I myself will journey
village to village, town to town,
paying homage to the Buddha,
and the clear rightness of the teaching!”

11.1.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi: “bhikkhavo”ti.
11.1.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. There the Buddha addressed the mendicants, “Mendicants!”

11.1.s: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ. Bhagavā etadavoca:
11.1.e: “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Buddha said this:
“Once upon a time, mendicants, the titans marched against the gods.

11.1.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi: ‘ete, tāta suvīra, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta suvīra, asure paccuyyāhī’ti.
11.1.e: Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed the godling Suvīra, ‘Dear Suvīra, the titans march against the gods! Go, and march against the titans!’

11.1.s: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, suvīro devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā pamādaṁ āpādesi.
11.1.e: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Suvīra. But he fell into negligence.

11.1.s: Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi: ‘ete, tāta suvīra, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta suvīra, asure paccuyyāhī’ti.
11.1.e: For a second time Sakka addressed Suvīra, ‘Dear Suvīra, the titans march against the gods! Go, and march against the titans!’

11.1.s: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, suvīro devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā dutiyampi pamādaṁ āpādesi.
11.1.e: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Suvīra. But for a second time he fell into negligence.

11.1.s: Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi: ‘ete, tāta suvīra, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta suvīra, asure paccuyyāhī’ti.
11.1.e: For a third time Sakka addressed Suvīra, ‘Dear Suvīra, the titans march against the gods! Go, and march against the titans!’

11.1.s: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, suvīro devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā tatiyampi pamādaṁ āpādesi.
11.1.e: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Suvīra. But for a third time he fell into negligence.

11.1.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo suvīraṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
11.1.e: Then Sakka addressed the godling Suvīra in verse:

11.1.s:
‘Anuṭṭhahaṁ avāyāmaṁ,
sukhaṁ yatrādhigacchati;
Suvīra tattha gacchāhi,
mañca tattheva pāpayā’ti.
11.1.e:
‘Suvīra, go to that place
where you can achieve happiness
without working for it or trying hard—
and take me with you!’

11.1.s:
‘Alasvassa anuṭṭhātā,
na ca kiccāni kāraye;
Sabbakāmasamiddhassa,
taṁ me sakka varaṁ disā’ti.
11.1.e:
‘That a lazy man who does no work,
and doesn’t do his duty,
can fulfill all his desires:
Sakka, render me this boon!’

11.1.s:
‘Yatthālaso anuṭṭhātā,
accantaṁ sukhamedhati;
Suvīra tattha gacchāhi,
mañca tattheva pāpayā’ti.
11.1.e:
‘Suvīra, go to that place
where a lazy man who does no work
prospers in unending happiness—
and take me with you!’

11.1.s:
‘Akammunā devaseṭṭha,
sakka vindemu yaṁ sukhaṁ;
Asokaṁ anupāyāsaṁ,
taṁ me sakka varaṁ disā’ti.
11.1.e:
‘O Sakka, first among gods,
that we might find the happiness
that’s sorrowless, unstressed:
Sakka, render me this boon!’

‘If there exists anywhere a place
where one can live happily without working,
that surely would be extinguishment’s path!
Go there, Suvīra,
and take me with you!’

11.1.s: So hi nāma, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sakaṁ puññaphalaṁ upajīvamāno devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kārento uṭṭhānavīriyassa vaṇṇavādī bhavissati. Idha kho taṁ, bhikkhave, sobhetha, yaṁ tumhe evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā uṭṭhaheyyātha ghaṭeyyātha vāyameyyātha appattassa pattiyā anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
11.1.e: Since, mendicants, even that Sakka, lord of gods—while living off of the fruit of his good deeds, and ruling as sovereign lord over these gods of the thirty-three—will speak in praise of initiative and energy, you can excel at this, for you who have gone forth in such a well explained teaching and training can try hard, strive, and make an effort to attain the unattained, achieve the unachieved, and realize the unrealized.”

11.2.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants, “Mendicants!”

11.2.s: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ. Bhagavā etadavoca:
11.2.e: “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Buddha said this:
“Once upon a time, mendicants, the titans marched against the gods.

11.2.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi: ‘ete, tāta susīma, asurā deve abhiyanti. Gaccha, tāta susīma, asure paccuyyāhī’ti.
11.2.e: Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed the godling Susīma, ‘Dear Susīma, the titans march against the gods! Go, and march against the titans!’

11.2.s: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, susīmo devaputto sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā pamādaṁ āpādesi.
11.2.e: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Susīma. But he fell into negligence.

11.2.s: Dutiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi …pe… dutiyampi pamādaṁ āpādesi.
Tatiyampi kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ āmantesi …pe… tatiyampi pamādaṁ āpādesi.
Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo susīmaṁ devaputtaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
11.2.e: Then Sakka addressed the godling Susīma in verse:

11.2.s:
‘Anuṭṭhahaṁ avāyāmaṁ,
sukhaṁ yatrādhigacchati;
Susīma tattha gacchāhi,
mañca tattheva pāpayā’ti.
11.2.e:
‘Susīma, go to that place
where you can achieve happiness
without working for it or trying hard—
and take me with you!’

11.2.s:
‘Alasvassa anuṭṭhātā,
na ca kiccāni kāraye;
Sabbakāmasamiddhassa,
taṁ me sakka varaṁ disā’ti.
11.2.e:
‘That a lazy man who does no work,
and doesn’t do his duty,
should fulfill all his desires:
Sakka, render me this boon!’

11.2.s:
‘Yatthālaso anuṭṭhātā,
accantaṁ sukhamedhati;
Susīma tattha gacchāhi,
mañca tattheva pāpayā’ti.
11.2.e:
‘Susīma, go to that place
where a lazy man who does no work
prospers in unending happiness—
and take me with you!’

11.2.s:
‘Akammunā devaseṭṭha,
sakka vindemu yaṁ sukhaṁ;
Asokaṁ anupāyāsaṁ,
taṁ me sakka varaṁ disā’ti.
11.2.e:
‘O Sakka, first among gods,
that we might find the happiness
that’s sorrowless, unstressed:
Sakka, render me this boon!’

‘If there exists anywhere a place
where one can live happily without working,
that surely would be extinguishment’s path!
Susīma, go to that place
and take me with you!’

11.2.s: So hi nāma, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sakaṁ puññaphalaṁ upajīvamāno devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kārento uṭṭhānavīriyassa vaṇṇavādī bhavissati. Idha kho taṁ, bhikkhave, sobhetha, yaṁ tumhe evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā uṭṭhaheyyātha ghaṭeyyātha vāyameyyātha appattassa pattiyā, anadhigatassa adhigamāya, asacchikatassa sacchikiriyāyā”ti.
11.2.e: Since, mendicants, even that Sakka, lord of gods—while living off of the fruit of his good deeds, and ruling as sovereign lord over these gods of the thirty-three—will speak in praise of initiative and energy, you can excel at this, for you who have gone forth in such a well explained teaching and training can try hard, strive, and make an effort to attain the unattained, achieve the unachieved, and realize the unrealized.”

11.3.e: There the Buddha addressed the mendicants, “Mendicants!”

11.3.s: “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṁ. Bhagavā etadavoca:
11.3.e: “Venerable sir,” they replied. The Buddha said this:

11.3.s: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi. Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo deve tāvatiṁse āmantesi:
11.3.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans. Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed the gods of the thirty-three:

11.3.s: ‘Sace, mārisā, devānaṁ saṅgāmagatānaṁ uppajjeyya bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, mameva tasmiṁ samaye dhajaggaṁ ullokeyyātha. Mamañhi vo dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyissati.
11.3.e: ‘Good fellows, when the gods are fighting, if you get scared or terrified, just look up at my banner’s crest. Then your fear and terror will go away.

11.3.s: No ce me dhajaggaṁ ullokeyyātha, atha pajāpatissa devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokeyyātha. Pajāpatissa hi vo devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyissati.
11.3.e: If you can’t see my banner’s crest, then look up at the banner’s crest of the Progenitor, king of gods. Then your fear and terror will go away.

11.3.s: No ce pajāpatissa devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokeyyātha, atha varuṇassa devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokeyyātha. Varuṇassa hi vo devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyissati.
11.3.e: If you can’t see his banner’s crest, then look up at the banner’s crest of Varuṇa, king of gods. Then your fear and terror will go away.

11.3.s: No ce varuṇassa devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokeyyātha, atha īsānassa devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokeyyātha. Īsānassa hi vo devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyissatī’ti.
11.3.e: If you can’t see his banner’s crest, then look up at the banner’s crest of Īsāna, king of gods. Then your fear and terror will go away.’

11.3.s: Taṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkassa vā devānamindassa dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ, pajāpatissa vā devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ, varuṇassa vā devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ, īsānassa vā devarājassa dhajaggaṁ ullokayataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyethāpi nopi pahīyetha.
11.3.e: However, when they look up at those banner’s crests their fear and terror might go away or it might not.

11.3.s: Taṁ kissa hetu? Sakko hi, bhikkhave, devānamindo avītarāgo avītadoso avītamoho bhīru chambhī utrāsī palāyīti.
11.3.e: Why is that? Because Sakka is not free of greed, hate, and delusion. He is fearful, scared, nervous, quick to flee.

11.3.s: Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, evaṁ vadāmi: ‘sace tumhākaṁ, bhikkhave, araññagatānaṁ vā rukkhamūlagatānaṁ vā suññāgāragatānaṁ vā uppajjeyya bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, mameva tasmiṁ samaye anussareyyātha: “itipi so bhagavā arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vijjācaraṇasampanno sugato lokavidū anuttaro purisadammasārathi satthā devamanussānaṁ buddho bhagavā”ti. Mamañhi vo, bhikkhave, anussarataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyissati.
11.3.e: But, mendicants, I say this: If you’ve gone to a wilderness, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty hut and you get scared or terrified, just recollect me: ‘That Blessed One is perfected, a fully awakened Buddha, accomplished in knowledge and conduct, holy, knower of the world, supreme guide for those fit for training, teacher of gods and humans, awakened, blessed.’ Then your fear and terror will go away.

11.3.s: No ce maṁ anussareyyātha, atha dhammaṁ anussareyyātha: “svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṁ veditabbo viññūhī”ti. Dhammañhi vo, bhikkhave, anussarataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyissati.
11.3.e: If you can’t recollect me, then recollect the teaching: ‘The teaching is well explained by the Buddha—apparent in the present life, immediately effective, inviting inspection, relevant, so that sensible people can know it for themselves.’ Then your fear and terror will go away.

11.3.s: No ce dhammaṁ anussareyyātha, atha saṅghaṁ anussareyyātha: “suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṁ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti. Saṅghañhi vo, bhikkhave, anussarataṁ yaṁ bhavissati bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā lomahaṁso vā, so pahīyissati.
11.3.e: If you can’t recollect the teaching, then recollect the Saṅgha: ‘The Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples is practicing the way that’s good, direct, systematic, and proper. It consists of the four pairs, the eight individual persons. This is the Saṅgha of the Buddha’s disciples that is worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and is the supreme field of merit for the world.’ Then your fear and terror will go away.

11.3.s: Taṁ kissa hetu? Tathāgato hi, bhikkhave, arahaṁ sammāsambuddho vītarāgo vītadoso vītamoho abhīru acchambhī anutrāsī apalāyī’”ti.
11.3.e: Why is that? Because the Realized One is free of greed, hate, and delusion. He is fearless, brave, bold, and stands his ground.”

11.3.s: Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṁ vatvāna sugato athāparaṁ etadavoca satthā:
11.3.e: That is what the Buddha said. Then the Holy One, the Teacher, went on to say:

11.3.s:
“Araññe rukkhamūle vā,
suññāgāreva bhikkhavo;
Anussaretha sambuddhaṁ,
bhayaṁ tumhāka no siyā.
11.3.e:
“In the wilderness, at a tree’s root,
or an empty hut, O mendicants,
recollect the Buddha,
and no fear will come to you.

11.3.s:
No ce buddhaṁ sareyyātha,
lokajeṭṭhaṁ narāsabhaṁ;
Atha dhammaṁ sareyyātha,
niyyānikaṁ sudesitaṁ.
11.3.e:
If you can’t recollect the Buddha—
the eldest in the world, the captain of men—
then recollect the teaching,
emancipating, well taught.

11.3.s:
No ce dhammaṁ sareyyātha,
niyyānikaṁ sudesitaṁ;
Atha saṅghaṁ sareyyātha,
puññakkhettaṁ anuttaraṁ.
11.3.e:
If you can’t recollect the teaching—
emancipating, well taught—
then recollect the Saṅgha,
the supreme field of merit.

11.3.s:
Evaṁ buddhaṁ sarantānaṁ,
Dhammaṁ saṅghañca bhikkhavo;
Bhayaṁ vā chambhitattaṁ vā,
Lomahaṁso na hessatī”ti.
11.3.e:
Thus recollecting the Buddha,
the teaching, and the Saṅgha, mendicants,
fear and terror
and goosebumps will be no more.”

11.4.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

11.4.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo asure āmantesi: ‘sace, mārisā, devānaṁ asurasaṅgāme samupabyūḷhe asurā jineyyuṁ devā parājineyyuṁ, yena naṁ sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi bandhitvā mama santike āneyyātha asurapuran’ti.
11.4.e: Then Vepacitti, lord of titans, addressed the titans, ‘My good fellows, if the titans defeat the gods in this battle, bind Sakka, the lord of gods, by his limbs and neck and bring him to my presence in the citadel of the titans.’

11.4.s: Sakkopi kho, bhikkhave, devānamindo deve tāvatiṁse āmantesi: ‘sace, mārisā, devānaṁ asurasaṅgāme samupabyūḷhe devā jineyyuṁ asurā parājineyyuṁ, yena naṁ vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi bandhitvā mama santike āneyyātha sudhammasabhan’ti.
11.4.e: Meanwhile, Sakka, lord of gods, addressed the gods of the thirty-three, ‘My good fellows, if the gods defeat the titans in this battle, bind Vepacitti by his limbs and neck and bring him to my presence in the Hall of Clear Right of the gods.’

11.4.s: Tasmiṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, saṅgāme devā jiniṁsu, asurā parājiniṁsu. Atha kho, bhikkhave, devā tāvatiṁsā vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi bandhitvā sakkassa devānamindassa santike ānesuṁ sudhammasabhaṁ.
11.4.e: In that battle the gods won and the titans lost. So the gods of the thirty-three bound Vepacitti by his limbs and neck and brought him to Sakka’s presence in the Hall of Clear Right of the gods.

11.4.s: Tatra sudaṁ, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo kaṇṭhapañcamehi bandhanehi baddho sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ sudhammasabhaṁ pavisantañca nikkhamantañca asabbhāhi pharusāhi vācāhi akkosati paribhāsati. Atha kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi:
11.4.e: And as Sakka was entering and leaving the hall, Vepacitti abused and insulted him with rude, harsh words. So Mātali the chariot handler addressed Sakka in verse:

11.4.s:
‘Bhayā nu maghavā sakka,
dubbalyā no titikkhasi;
Suṇanto pharusaṁ vācaṁ,
sammukhā vepacittino’ti.
11.4.e:
‘O Maghavā, O Sakka,
is it from fear or from weakness
that you endure such harsh words
in the presence of Vepacitti?’

11.4.s:
‘Nāhaṁ bhayā na dubbalyā,
khamāmi vepacittino;
Kathañhi mādiso viññū,
bālena paṭisaṁyuje’ti.
11.4.e:
‘It’s not out of fear or weakness
that I’m patient with Vepacitti.
For how can a sensible person like me
get in a fight with a fool?’

11.4.s:
‘Bhiyyo bālā pabhijjeyyuṁ,
no cassa paṭisedhako;
Tasmā bhusena daṇḍena,
dhīro bālaṁ nisedhaye’ti.
11.4.e:
‘Fools would vent even more
if there’s no one to put a stop to them.
So an attentive one should stop
a fool with forceful punishment.’

11.4.s:
‘Etadeva ahaṁ maññe,
bālassa paṭisedhanaṁ;
Paraṁ saṅkupitaṁ ñatvā,
yo sato upasammatī’ti.
11.4.e:
‘I think that this is the only way
to put a stop to a fool,
when you know that the other is upset,
be mindful and stay calm.’

‘In this mere endurance, Vāsava,
I see a flaw.
When a fool thinks,
“He endures me out of fear,”
the simpleton will go after you even harder,
like a cow chasing someone who runs away.’

11.4.s:
‘Kāmaṁ maññatu vā mā vā,
bhayā myāyaṁ titikkhati;
Sadatthaparamā atthā,
khantyā bhiyyo na vijjati.
11.4.e:
‘Let him think this if he wishes, or not—
“He endures me out of fear.”
For the highest goal, one’s own,
naught better than patience is found.

11.4.s:
Yo have balavā santo,
dubbalassa titikkhati;
Tamāhu paramaṁ khantiṁ,
niccaṁ khamati dubbalo.
11.4.e:
When a strong person
endures a weakling,
they call that the ultimate patience,
for a weakling must always be patient.

11.4.s:
Abalaṁ taṁ balaṁ āhu,
yassa bālabalaṁ balaṁ;
Balassa dhammaguttassa,
paṭivattā na vijjati.
11.4.e:
The strength of folly
is really just weakness, they say.
But no one can challenge a person
who’s strong, guarded by the teaching.

11.4.s:
Tasseva tena pāpiyo,
yo kuddhaṁ paṭikujjhati;
Kuddhaṁ appaṭikujjhanto,
saṅgāmaṁ jeti dujjayaṁ.
11.4.e:
When you get angry at an angry person
you just make things worse for yourself.
When you don’t get angry at an angry person
you win a battle hard to win.

11.4.s:
Ubhinnamatthaṁ carati,
attano ca parassa ca;
Paraṁ saṅkupitaṁ ñatvā,
yo sato upasammati.
11.4.e:
When you know that the other is angry,
you act for the good of both
yourself and the other
if you’re mindful and stay calm.

11.4.s:
Ubhinnaṁ tikicchantānaṁ,
attano ca parassa ca;
Janā maññanti bāloti,
ye dhammassa akovidā’ti.
11.4.e:
People inexpert in the teaching
consider one who heals both
oneself and the other
to be a fool.’

11.4.s: So hi nāma, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo sakaṁ puññaphalaṁ upajīvamāno devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kārento khantisoraccassa vaṇṇavādī bhavissati. Idha kho taṁ, bhikkhave, sobhetha yaṁ tumhe evaṁ svākkhāte dhammavinaye pabbajitā samānā khamā ca bhaveyyātha soratā cā”ti.
11.4.e: Since, mendicants, even that Sakka, lord of gods—while living off of the fruit of his good deeds, and ruling as sovereign lord over these gods of the thirty-three—will speak in praise of patience and gentleness, you can excel at this, for you who have gone forth in such a well explained teaching and training can develop patience and gentleness.”

11.5.s: Sāvatthinidānaṁ.
11.5.e: At Sāvatthī.

11.5.s: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi.
11.5.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

11.5.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca: ‘hotu, devānaminda, subhāsitena jayo’ti.
11.5.e: Then Vepacitti, lord of titans, said to Sakka, lord of gods, ‘Lord of gods, let there be victory by fine words!’

11.5.s: ‘Hotu, vepacitti, subhāsitena jayo’ti.
11.5.e: ‘Vepacitti, let there be victory by fine words!’

11.5.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, devā ca asurā ca pārisajje ṭhapesuṁ: ‘ime no subhāsitadubbhāsitaṁ ājānissantī’ti.
11.5.e: Then the gods and the titans appointed a panel of judges, saying, ‘These will understand our good and bad statements.’

11.5.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca: ‘bhaṇa, devānaminda, gāthan’ti.
11.5.e: Then Vepacitti, lord of titans, said to Sakka, lord of gods, ‘Lord of gods, recite a verse!’

11.5.s: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ etadavoca: ‘tumhe khvettha, vepacitti, pubbadevā. Bhaṇa, vepacitti, gāthan’ti.
11.5.e: When he said this, Sakka said to him, ‘Vepacitti, you are the elder gods here. Recite a verse.’

11.5.s: Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
11.5.e: So Vepacitti spoke this verse:

11.5.s:
‘Bhiyyo bālā pabhijjeyyuṁ,
no cassa paṭisedhako;
Tasmā bhusena daṇḍena,
dhīro bālaṁ nisedhaye’ti.
11.5.e:
‘Fools would vent even more
if there’s no one to put a stop to them.
So an intelligent person should stop
a fool with forceful punishment.’

11.5.s: Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, vepacittinā asurindena gāthāya asurā anumodiṁsu, devā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
11.5.e: The titans applauded Vepacitti’s verse, while the gods kept silent.

11.5.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca: ‘bhaṇa, devānaminda, gāthan’ti. Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
11.5.e: Then Vepacitti said to Sakka, ‘Lord of gods, recite a verse!’ So Sakka spoke this verse:

11.5.s:
‘Etadeva ahaṁ maññe,
bālassa paṭisedhanaṁ;
Paraṁ saṅkupitaṁ ñatvā,
yo sato upasammatī’ti.
11.5.e:
‘I think that this is the only way
to put a stop to a fool,
when you know that the other is upset,
be mindful and stay calm.’

11.5.s: Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkena devānamindena gāthāya, devā anumodiṁsu, asurā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
11.5.e: The gods applauded Sakka’s verse, while the titans kept silent.

11.5.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ etadavoca: ‘bhaṇa, vepacitti, gāthan’ti. Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
11.5.e: Then Sakka said to Vepacitti, ‘Vepacitti, recite a verse!’ So Vepacitti spoke this verse:

‘In this mere endurance, Vāsava,
I see a flaw.
When a fool thinks,
“He endures me out of fear,”
the simpleton will go after you even harder,
like a cow chasing someone who runs away.’

11.5.s: Bhāsitāya kho pana, bhikkhave, vepacittinā asurindena gāthāya asurā anumodiṁsu, devā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
11.5.e: The titans applauded Vepacitti’s verse, while the gods kept silent.

11.5.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ etadavoca: ‘bhaṇa, devānaminda, gāthan’ti. Evaṁ vutte, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo imā gāthāyo abhāsi:
11.5.e: Then Vepacitti said to Sakka, ‘Lord of gods, recite a verse!’ So Sakka spoke this verse:

11.5.s:
‘Kāmaṁ maññatu vā mā vā,
bhayā myāyaṁ titikkhati;
Sadatthaparamā atthā,
khantyā bhiyyo na vijjati.
11.5.e:
‘Let him think this if he wishes, or not—
“He endures me out of fear.”
For the highest goal, one’s own,
naught better than patience is found.

11.5.s:
Yo have balavā santo,
dubbalassa titikkhati;
Tamāhu paramaṁ khantiṁ,
niccaṁ khamati dubbalo.
11.5.e:
When a strong person
endures a weakling,
they call that the ultimate patience,
for a weakling must always be patient.

11.5.s:
Abalaṁ taṁ balaṁ āhu,
yassa bālabalaṁ balaṁ;
Balassa dhammaguttassa,
paṭivattā na vijjati.
11.5.e:
The strength of folly
is really just weakness, they say.
But no one can challenge a person
who’s strong, guarded by the teaching.

11.5.s:
Tasseva tena pāpiyo,
yo kuddhaṁ paṭikujjhati;
Kuddhaṁ appaṭikujjhanto,
saṅgāmaṁ jeti dujjayaṁ.
11.5.e:
When you get angry at an angry person
you just make things worse for yourself.
When you don’t get angry at an angry person
you win a battle hard to win.

11.5.s:
Ubhinnamatthaṁ carati,
attano ca parassa ca;
Paraṁ saṅkupitaṁ ñatvā,
yo sato upasammati.
11.5.e:
When you know that the other is angry,
you act for the good of both
yourself and the other
if you’re mindful and stay calm.

11.5.s:
Ubhinnaṁ tikicchantānaṁ,
attano ca parassa ca;
Janā maññanti bāloti,
ye dhammassa akovidā’ti.
11.5.e:
People inexpert in the teaching
consider one who heals both
oneself and the other
to be a fool.’

11.5.s: Bhāsitāsu kho pana, bhikkhave, sakkena devānamindena gāthāsu, devā anumodiṁsu, asurā tuṇhī ahesuṁ.
11.5.e: The gods applauded Sakka’s verses, while the titans kept silent.

11.5.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, devānañca asurānañca pārisajjā etadavocuṁ: ‘bhāsitā kho vepacittinā asurindena gāthāyo. Tā ca kho sadaṇḍāvacarā sasatthāvacarā, iti bhaṇḍanaṁ iti viggaho iti kalaho. Bhāsitā kho sakkena devānamindena gāthāyo. Tā ca kho adaṇḍāvacarā asatthāvacarā, iti abhaṇḍanaṁ iti aviggaho iti akalaho.
11.5.e: Then the panel of judges consisting of both gods and titans said this, ‘The verses spoken by Vepacitti evoke punishment and violence. That’s how you get fights, arguments, and quarrels. The verses spoken by Sakka don’t evoke punishment and violence. That’s how you stay free of fights, arguments, and quarrels.

11.5.s: Sakkassa devānamindassa subhāsitena jayo’ti.
11.5.e: Sakka, lord of gods, wins victory by fine words!’

11.5.s: Iti kho, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa subhāsitena jayo ahosī”ti.
11.5.e: And that’s how Sakka came to win victory by fine words.”

11.6.s: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi. Tasmiṁ kho pana, bhikkhave, saṅgāme asurā jiniṁsu, devā parājiniṁsu. Parājitā ca kho, bhikkhave, devā apāyaṁsveva uttarenamukhā, abhiyaṁsveva ne asurā.
11.6.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, a battle was fought between the gods and the titans. In that battle the titans won and the gods lost. Defeated, the gods fled north with the titans in pursuit.

11.6.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo mātali saṅgāhakaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsi:
11.6.e: Then Sakka, lord of gods, addressed his chariot handler Mātali in verse:

11.6.s:
‘Kulāvakā mātali simbalismiṁ,
Īsāmukhena parivajjayassu;
Kāmaṁ cajāma asuresu pāṇaṁ,
Māyime dijā vikulāvakā ahesun’ti.
11.6.e:
‘Mātali, don’t ram the bird nests
in the Red Silk-Cotton Woods with your draft-pole.
I’d rather give up our lives to the titans
than deprive these birds of their nests.’

11.6.s: ‘Evaṁ, bhaddantavā’ti kho, bhikkhave, mātali saṅgāhako sakkassa devānamindassa paṭissutvā sahassayuttaṁ ājaññarathaṁ paccudāvattesi.
11.6.e: ‘Yes, lord,’ replied Mātali. And he turned the chariot back around, with its team of a thousand thoroughbreds.

11.6.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, asurānaṁ etadahosi: ‘paccudāvatto kho dāni sakkassa devānamindassa sahassayutto ājaññaratho. Dutiyampi kho devā asurehi saṅgāmessantī’ti bhītā asurapurameva pāvisiṁsu.
11.6.e: Then the titans thought, ‘Now Sakka’s chariot has turned back. The titans will have to fight the gods a second time!’ Terrified, they retreated right away to the citadel of the titans.

11.6.s: Iti kho, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa dhammena jayo ahosī”ti.
11.6.e: And that’s how Sakka came to win victory by principle.”

11.7.s: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, sakkassa devānamindassa rahogatassa paṭisallīnassa evaṁ cetaso parivitakko udapādi: ‘yopi me assa supaccatthiko tassapāhaṁ na dubbheyyan’ti.
11.7.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, as Sakka, lord of gods, was in private retreat this thought came to his mind, ‘I should never betray even a sworn enemy.’

11.7.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo sakkassa devānamindassa cetasā cetoparivitakkamaññāya yena sakko devānamindo tenupasaṅkami.
11.7.e: And then Vepacitti, lord of titans, knowing Sakka’s train of thought, approached him.

11.7.s: Addasā kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ. Disvāna vepacittiṁ asurindaṁ etadavoca: ‘tiṭṭha, vepacitti, gahitosī’ti.
11.7.e: Sakka saw Vepacitti coming off in the distance, and said to him, ‘Stop, Vepacitti, you’re caught!’

11.7.s: ‘Yadeva te, mārisa, pubbe cittaṁ, tadeva tvaṁ mā pajahāsī’ti.
11.7.e: ‘Good fellow, don’t give up the idea you just had!’
‘Swear, Vepacitti, that you won’t betray me.’

‘Whatever bad things happen to a liar,
or to someone who slanders the noble ones,
or to someone who betrays a friend,
or to someone who’s ungrateful,
the same bad things impact
anyone who betrays you, Sujā’s husband.’”

11.8.s: Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā divāvihāragato hoti paṭisallīno.
11.8.e: Now at that time the Buddha had gone into retreat for the day’s meditation.

11.8.s: Atha kho sakko ca devānamindo verocano ca asurindo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā paccekaṁ dvārabāhaṁ nissāya aṭṭhaṁsu. Atha kho verocano asurindo bhagavato santike imaṁ gāthaṁ abhāsi:
11.8.e: Then Sakka, lord of gods, and Verocana, lord of titans, approached the Buddha and stationed themselves one by each door-post. Then Verocana spoke this verse in the Buddha’s presence:

11.8.s:
“Vāyametheva puriso,
yāva atthassa nipphadā;
Nipphannasobhano attho,
verocanavaco idan”ti.
11.8.e:
“A man should make an effort
until his goal is accomplished.
A goal is splendid when accomplished—
this is the word of Verocana!”

11.8.s:
“Vāyametheva puriso,
yāva atthassa nipphadā;
Nipphannasobhano attho,
khantyā bhiyyo na vijjatī”ti.
11.8.e:
“A man should make an effort
until his goal is accomplished.
For the goal that’s splendid when accomplished,
naught better than patience is found.”

“All beings are in need,
as they deserve in each case.
But even so, harnessed work is the highest
thing of value for all living creatures.
A goal is splendid when accomplished—
this is the word of Verocana!”

“All beings are in need,
as they deserve in each case.
But rather than harnessed work being the highest
thing of value for all living creatures,
for the goal that’s splendid when accomplished,
naught better than patience is found.”

11.9.s: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, sambahulā isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā araññāyatane paṇṇakuṭīsu sammanti.
11.9.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, several seers who were ethical, of good character, settled in leaf huts in a wilderness region.

11.9.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko ca devānamindo vepacitti ca asurindo yena te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu. Atha kho, bhikkhave, vepacitti asurindo paṭaliyo upāhanā ārohitvā khaggaṁ olaggetvā chattena dhāriyamānena aggadvārena assamaṁ pavisitvā te isayo sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme apabyāmato karitvā atikkami.
11.9.e: Then Sakka, lord of gods, and Vepacitti, lord of titans, went to those seers. Vepacitti put on his lined sandals, strapped on his sword, and, carrying a sunshade, entered the hermitage through the main gate. He walked right past those seers, keeping them at arm’s length.

11.9.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sakko devānamindo paṭaliyo upāhanā orohitvā khaggaṁ aññesaṁ datvā chattaṁ apanāmetvā dvāreneva assamaṁ pavisitvā te isayo sīlavante kalyāṇadhamme anuvātaṁ pañjaliko namassamāno aṭṭhāsi.
11.9.e: Sakka took off his lined sandals, gave his sword to others, and, putting down his sunshade, entered the hermitage through the same gate. He stood downwind of those seers, revering them with cupped palms.

11.9.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā sakkaṁ devānamindaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsiṁsu:
11.9.e: Then those seers addressed Sakka in verse:

11.9.s:
‘Gandho isīnaṁ ciradikkhitānaṁ,
Kāyā cuto gacchati mālutena;
Ito paṭikkamma sahassanetta,
Gandho isīnaṁ asuci devarājā’ti.
11.9.e:
‘When seers have been long initiated,
the odor of their bodies goes with the gale.
You’d better leave, O thousand-eyed!
The odor of the seers is unclean, king of gods.’

‘When seers have been long initiated,
let the odor of their bodies go with the gale.
We yearn for this odor, sirs,
like a colorful crown of flowers.
The gods don’t see it as repulsive.’”

11.10.s: “Bhūtapubbaṁ, bhikkhave, sambahulā isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā samuddatīre paṇṇakuṭīsu sammanti.
11.10.e: “Once upon a time, mendicants, several seers who were ethical, of good character, settled in leaf huts on the ocean shore.

11.10.s: Tena kho pana samayena devāsurasaṅgāmo samupabyūḷho ahosi.
11.10.e: Now at that time a battle was fought between the gods and the titans.

11.10.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, tesaṁ isīnaṁ sīlavantānaṁ kalyāṇadhammānaṁ etadahosi: ‘dhammikā kho devā, adhammikā asurā. Siyāpi no asurato bhayaṁ. Yannūna mayaṁ sambaraṁ asurindaṁ upasaṅkamitvā abhayadakkhiṇaṁ yāceyyāmā’ti.
11.10.e: Then the seers thought, ‘The gods are principled, the titans are unprincipled. We may be at risk from the titans. Why don’t we approach Sambara, lord of titans, and beg him for a pledge of safety?’

11.10.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—samuddatīre paṇṇakuṭīsu antarahitā sambarassa asurindassa sammukhe pāturahesuṁ. Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā sambaraṁ asurindaṁ gāthāya ajjhabhāsiṁsu:
11.10.e: Then, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, those seers vanished from those leaf huts on the ocean shore and reappeared in Sambara’s presence. Then those seers addressed Sambara in verse:

11.10.s:
‘Isayo sambaraṁ pattā,
yācanti abhayadakkhiṇaṁ;
Kāmaṅkaro hi te dātuṁ,
bhayassa abhayassa vā’ti.
11.10.e:
‘The seers have come to Sambara
to beg for a pledge of safety.
For you can give them what you wish,
whether danger or safety.’

11.10.s:
‘Isīnaṁ abhayaṁ natthi,
duṭṭhānaṁ sakkasevinaṁ;
Abhayaṁ yācamānānaṁ,
bhayameva dadāmi vo’ti.
11.10.e:
‘There is no safety for seers,
the hated associates of Sakka!
Though you beg me for your safety,
I’ll only give you fear!’

11.10.s:
‘Abhayaṁ yācamānānaṁ,
bhayameva dadāsi no;
Paṭiggaṇhāma te etaṁ,
akkhayaṁ hotu te bhayaṁ.
11.10.e:
‘Though we beg you for our safety,
you give us only fear.
This is what we get from you:
may endless peril come to you!

Whatever kind of seed you sow,
that is the fruit you reap.
A doer of good gets good,
a doer of bad gets bad.
You, my dear, have sown your own seed,
now you’ll experience the fruit.’

11.10.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, te isayo sīlavanto kalyāṇadhammā sambaraṁ asurindaṁ abhisapitvā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evameva—sambarassa asurindassa sammukhe antarahitā samuddatīre paṇṇakuṭīsu pāturahesuṁ.
11.10.e: Then those seers, having cursed Sambara, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Sambara’s presence and reappeared in those leaf huts on the ocean shore.

11.10.s: Atha kho, bhikkhave, sambaro asurindo tehi isīhi sīlavantehi kalyāṇadhammehi abhisapito rattiyā sudaṁ tikkhattuṁ ubbijjī”ti.
11.10.e: But after being cursed by the seers, Sambara woke in alarm three times that night.”

11.11.s: “Sakkassa, bhikkhave, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa satta vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṁ, yesaṁ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṁ ajjhagā. Katamāni satta vatapadāni?
11.11.e: “Mendicants, in a former life, when Sakka was a human being, he undertook seven vows. And it was because of undertaking these that he achieved the status of Sakka. What seven?

11.11.s: Yāvajīvaṁ mātāpettibharo assaṁ, yāvajīvaṁ kule jeṭṭhāpacāyī assaṁ, yāvajīvaṁ saṇhavāco assaṁ, yāvajīvaṁ apisuṇavāco assaṁ, yāvajīvaṁ vigatamalamaccherena cetasā agāraṁ ajjhāvaseyyaṁ muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṁvibhāgarato, yāvajīvaṁ saccavāco assaṁ, yāvajīvaṁ akkodhano assaṁ—sacepi me kodho uppajjeyya, khippameva naṁ paṭivineyyanti.
11.11.e: As long as I live, may I support my parents. As long as I live, may I honor the elders in the family. As long as I live, may I speak gently. As long as I live, may I not backbite. As long as I live, may I live at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share. As long as I live, may I speak the truth. As long as I live, may I be free of anger, or should anger arise, may I quickly get rid of it.

11.11.s: Sakkassa, bhikkhave, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa imāni satta vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṁ, yesaṁ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṁ ajjhagāti.
11.11.e: In a former life, when Sakka was a human being, he undertook seven vows. And it was because of undertaking these that he achieved the status of Sakka.

11.11.s:
Mātāpettibharaṁ jantuṁ,
kule jeṭṭhāpacāyinaṁ;
Saṇhaṁ sakhilasambhāsaṁ,
pesuṇeyyappahāyinaṁ.
11.11.e:
A child who respects their parents,
and honors the elders in the family,
whose speech is gentle and courteous,
and has given up backbiting;

11.11.s:
Maccheravinaye yuttaṁ,
saccaṁ kodhābhibhuṁ naraṁ;
Taṁ ve devā tāvatiṁsā,
āhu sappuriso itī”ti.
11.11.e:
who’s committed to getting rid of stinginess,
is truthful, and has mastered anger:
the gods of the thirty-three declare
them to be a true person.”

11.12.s: Sāvatthiyaṁ jetavane. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū etadavoca:
11.12.e: Near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove. There the Buddha said to the mendicants:

11.12.s: “sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno magho nāma māṇavo ahosi, tasmā maghavāti vuccati.
11.12.e: “Mendicants, in a former life, when Sakka was a human being, he was a student named Magha. That’s why he’s called Maghavā, the Bounteous.

11.12.s: Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno pure dānaṁ adāsi, tasmā purindadoti vuccati.
11.12.e: In a former life, when Sakka was a human being, he was first to give gifts. That’s why he’s called Purindada, the Firstgiver.

11.12.s: Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno sakkaccaṁ dānaṁ adāsi, tasmā sakkoti vuccati.
11.12.e: In a former life, when Sakka was a human being, he gave gifts ably. That’s why he’s called Sakka, the Able.

11.12.s: Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno āvasathaṁ adāsi, tasmā vāsavoti vuccati.
11.12.e: In a former life, when Sakka was a human being, he gave the gift of a guest house. That’s why he’s called Vāsava, the Houser.

11.12.s: Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo sahassampi atthānaṁ muhuttena cinteti, tasmā sahassakkhoti vuccati.
11.12.e: Sakka thinks of a thousand needs in an hour. That’s why he’s called Sahassakkha, the Thousand-Eyed.

11.12.e: Sakka’s wife is the titan maiden named Sujā. That’s why he’s called Sujampati, Sujā’s Husband.

11.12.s: Sakko, bhikkhave, devānamindo devānaṁ tāvatiṁsānaṁ issariyādhipaccaṁ rajjaṁ kāreti, tasmā devānamindoti vuccati.

A child who respects their parents,

11.13.s: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
11.13.e: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Vesālī, at the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

11.13.s: Atha kho mahāli licchavī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho mahāli licchavī bhagavantaṁ etadavoca: “Diṭṭho kho, bhante, bhagavatā sakko devānamindo”ti?
11.13.e: Then Mahāli the Licchavi went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him, “Sir, have you seen Sakka, lord of gods?”

11.13.s: “So hi nūna, bhante, sakkapatirūpako bhavissati. Duddaso hi, bhante, sakko devānamindo”ti.
11.13.e: “But surely, sir, you must have seen someone who looked like Sakka. For Sakka is hard to see.”

11.13.s: “Sakkañca khvāhaṁ, mahāli, pajānāmi sakkakaraṇe ca dhamme, yesaṁ dhammānaṁ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṁ ajjhagā, tañca pajānāmi.
11.13.e: “Mahāli, I understand Sakka. And I understand the things that he undertook and committed to, which enabled him to achieve the status of Sakka.

11.13.s: Sakko, mahāli, devānamindo pubbe manussabhūto samāno magho nāma māṇavo ahosi, tasmā maghavāti vuccati.
11.13.e: In a former life, when Sakka was a human being, he was a student named Magha. That’s why he’s called Maghavā, the Bounteous.

11.13.e: As long as I live, may I support my parents. As long as I live, may I honor the elders in the family. As long as I live, may I speak gently. As long as I live, may I not backbite. As long as I live, may I live at home with heart rid of the stain of stinginess, freely generous, open-handed, loving to let go, committed to charity, loving to give and to share. As long as I live, may I speak the truth. As long as I live, may I be free of anger, or should anger arise, may I quickly get rid of it.

11.13.s: Sakkassa, mahāli, devānamindassa pubbe manussabhūtassa imāni satta vatapadāni samattāni samādinnāni ahesuṁ, yesaṁ samādinnattā sakko sakkattaṁ ajjhagāti.

Mātāpettibharaṁ jantuṁ,
kule jeṭṭhāpacāyinaṁ;
Saṇhaṁ sakhilasambhāsaṁ,

and honors the elders in the family,

who’s committed to getting rid of stinginess,
